Subject: Intro + question on founder stipend and invoicing path

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team and I liked the latency guarantees you shared. We're finalizing our accelerator package and I had a practical bookkeeping question: the program provides a $15k stipend per cohort company that can be used as credits on Redwood. Is that stipend treated as a prepaid credit (applied up front against invoices) or as a promotional monthly allowance that shows as a discount on each invoice? Our finance lead also needs to know whether the stipend can be invoiced to the accelerator and then transferred to the founders, or if Redwood requires the credits to be attached to the founders' accounts directly.

I'm attaching our proposed SOW and a simple one-pager of how we did this with another vendor — curious if Redwood can match that flow. Can we jump on a quick call today or tomorrow to align?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Intro + question on founder stipend and invoicing path

Hi Mina — great to hear from you. Short answer: we support both flows, but there are operational differences and accounting implications.

High-level options:
- Accelerator-billed stipend: Redwood invoices the accelerator for a prepaid block of credits (e.g., $15k per company), and you can allocate/redemptions to the cohort companies from your admin console. This is simplest for sponsorship accounting but requires a prepayment or monthly invoicing arrangement.
- Per-founder credit assignment: Credits are issued directly to each founder's account (no transfer necessary). Invoices for each account will show normal usage; the stipend appears as a credit balance that reduces charges.

Key tradeoffs we should confirm on the call: whether you need a single invoice per cohort (for your accounting) vs individual invoices per company (for founders). Also need to confirm VAT/tax treatment and whether you want credits to expire or roll over.

Looping in Ben (Sales ops) to propose packaging/discounting options and Laura (Finance ops) to advise on invoicing mechanics. Ben — can you sketch two packaging options we can propose (prepaid cohort pool vs per-founder allocation) and a sample invoice mock?

I can do a 30 min sync 11:30am PT today or 9am PT tomorrow. Which works for you?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Mina — thanks for the background and the SOW. I attached a quick proposal (SparkFounders_Proposal_v2.pdf) with two paths and a sample invoice line. Summary:

Path A — Prepaid cohort pool
- Accelerator signs a prepaid invoice for $15k x N companies up front.
- Redwood issues a pooled credit bucket owned by SparkFounders; program admins can assign credits to founder accounts.
- Pros: single invoice for your org, straightforward sponsor accounting.
- Cons: requires prepayment or net-30 invoice for the full cohort; credits expire after 12 months by default (can be adjusted).

Path B — Direct founder credits + promo top-up
- Each founder receives $15k of promo credits applied to their account.
- Redwood invoices founders directly for any overages beyond the stipend, or you can set a % discount plan for conversions to Dedicated.
- Pros: founders keep simple billing; no chargebacks.
- Cons: harder for your finance team to reconcile at scale if you want a single sponsor invoice.

Operational questions for finance team:
- Do you need 1099/recipients or will the stipend be categorized as service credits?
- If you prefer Path A with sponsor invoicing, what payment term do you require (prepaid, net-30, net-60)?

Laura — can you confirm the internal approval needed to create a sponsor-owned pooled credit product and the tax/invoice fields we must include on the cohort invoice?

Mina — happy to review the two options on the call. I penciled you for 11:30am PT today on Aditya's note; if that doesn't work we'll pick tomorrow AM.

— Ben
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SparkFounders_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — quick finance notes so Mina and SparkFounders can plan:

1) Sponsor-owned pooled credits (Path A)
- Accounting treatment: we issue a prepaid invoice to the sponsor; that payment is recognized as deferred revenue on Redwood's books and drawn down as credits are consumed by founders. We can include a memo line that references each cohort or batch id for your internal reconciliation.
- Tax/invoice needs: we need a billing contact, tax-id for your organization, and purchase order number if you require one. For US domestic sponsors we default to net-30; net-60 can be approved for >$100k with procurement sign-off.

2) Direct per-founder credits (Path B)
- Accounting treatment: credits are applied to the founders' accounts; invoices are generated at the account level. If SparkFounders prefers to reimburse founders, that's an off-platform arrangement.

3) Expense reporting and 1099s
- If founders are US individuals receiving stipend monies as taxable compensation, your counsel should advise; Redwood treats promo credits as non-cash credits on our platform. We do not issue 1099s for credits.

Next steps I need from SparkFounders to prepare a sponsor invoice template: billing name, billing address, tax-id (EIN), PO number (if used), billing contact name/email, cohort id. Also confirm desired expiry window for credits (12/18/24 months).

Mina — if you share that info now I can spin a sample invoice and a sample accounting memo we can include on your AR ledger.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
